report.summary: Analyzed chunk 5 of vendors.py: defines _CLAUDE_DENIED_TOOLS, COUNCIL_PROFILES, _assert_profile_safe, CouncilAdapter class with __init__ and assemble method. Verified claims about tool denial, profile safety, and adapter design against visible code.
risks: _CLAUDE_DENIED_TOOLS | low | The string contains commas but no spaces after commas; tools like 'Bash,Edit' might be parsed as a single tool name by the CLI, potentially bypassing denial. | Check the actual parsing of --disallowed-tools by the claude CLI.

claims.text: "--allowed-tools <tools...>" would swallow the next flag if given an empty value, so the denial is expressed with the ``=`` form, which cannot slurp.
claims.why: The claim explains a design decision but does not reference any code in this chunk that demonstrates the slurping behavior. The actual parsing is external.

claims.text: tools denied, MCP pinned to the empty --mcp-config set.
claims.why: The comment says MCP is pinned to empty --mcp-config set, but the profile's args include '--strict-mcp-config' without a value, which likely expects a following argument. The empty set is not represented in the visible args.

claims.text: read-only sandbox + approvals never; --skip-git-repo-check because the council cwd is a bare temp dir by design and codex otherwise refuses.
claims.why: The openai profile includes '--sandbox', 'read-only', '--ask-for-approval', 'never', and '--skip-git-repo-check' in args, matching the comment.

claims.text: a council member reviews, it never writes
claims.why: The claim about policy is not verifiable from this code; no forbidden fragments list is shown.

claims.text: ``ask`` is the ONLY entry point, and it always: charges the token ceiling, runs the secret floor, computes withheld paths for an untrusted lane, times the call, and maps every failure onto :data:`STATUSES`.
claims.why: The method ask is not defined in this chunk, so its behavior cannot be verified.

claims.text: A refusal is a STATUS, not an exception -- a council must never lose a participant to a traceback, because a missing turn is indistinguishable from a turn that was never sought.
claims.why: No code in this chunk implements refusal handling or status mapping.

claims.text: The adapter -- not the caller -- renders the evidence blocks, because a gate that only REPORTS withheld paths while the caller ships the bytes anyway is worse than no gate: it produces a record saying the council did not see a file it did in fact see.
claims.why: The assemble method signature shows it takes withheld paths, but the actual rendering logic is not visible in this chunk.

observations.what: _CLAUDE_DENIED_TOOLS is a single string with no spaces after commas; the CLI may parse it as multiple tools or a single tool name depending on separator handling.
The anthropic profile includes '--strict-mcp-config' without a value, which may cause the CLI to expect a following argument; the comment claims it's empty but no empty value is provided.
The openai profile uses 'exec' as a subcommand and '-' to read from stdin; the comment does not mention 'exec' or stdin.
The _assert_profile_safe function is called on all profiles at module load, but the forbidden fragments list (FORBIDDEN_ARG_FRAGMENTS) is not defined in this chunk.
